items.label: text
items.text: In an experiment to find the empirical formula of lead oxide, a small porcelain dish was weighed, filled with lead oxide and weighed again. The dish was placed in a tube and heated in a stream of hydrogen. The hydrogen reduced the lead oxide to a bead of metallic lead. When the apparatus was cool, the dish and its bead of lead were weighed together.

items.label: text
items.text: Mass of porcelain dish + lead oxide = 24.80 g

items.label: text
items.text: Mass of porcelain dish + lead = 24.16 g

items.label: list_item
items.text: a Calculate the mass of lead in the lead oxide. (1)

items.label: list_item
items.text: b Calculate the mass of oxygen in the lead oxide. (1)

items.label: list_item
items.text: c There are three different oxides of lead: PbO, PbO2 and PbO4. Use your results from a and b to find the empirical formula of the oxide used in the experiment. (ε)
